text: We will support companies in their sustainability journey through the green economy pillar.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They can both do well and do good, particularly as consumers and investors increasingly prioritise sustainability.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This includes working with our researchers and companies to develop new solutions that push the frontiers on sustainability, such as through the Research Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2025 plan.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As part of Singapore Together and to involve every Singaporean in the movement, as Ms Hany Soh, Miss Cheryl Chan have highlighted, the Government will launch a series of Green Plan Conversations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This is part of our efforts to partner, encourage, and support ground-up efforts and catalyse new partnerships.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Projects in line with the Green Plan, and Alliances for Action will be launched in the coming months.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Hany Soh asked about the current progress of the fund.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are evaluating the proposals and I look forward to sharing about them in the coming months.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: (In Malay):   Climate change poses grave threats for Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Last year was one of the hottest ever, with frequent and heavy rainfall events.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We need to make deep transformations in all aspects of our lives and work together to tackle climate change.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To chart our pathway to a sustainable future, the Government has launched the Singapore Green Plan 2030, for a whole-of-nation action.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Everyone, regardless of age, race, and background can and must play a part.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As individuals, we can change our daily habits, by consuming and wasting less resources, recycling more, taking public transport where we can, or turning our air-conditioner up by one degree higher.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As businesses, we can use less packaging materials, adopt energy and water efficient manufacturing processes, and recycle our waste better, into useful resources.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The public sector will drive a nation-wide push towards sustainability using the tools and levers at our disposal, such as green procurement.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our children' future depends on what we do today, to preserve our resources and protect the earth.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Let us work together to make Singapore a City of Green Possibilities.

text: Our children's future depends on what we do today, to preserve our natural resources and protect the earth.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Let us work together to make Singapore a City of Green Possibilities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: A few months ago, I was struck by a question from my son.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: He asked if I would still have had children, given how our planet is struggling to support a growing population, with the daunting challenges that climate change will pose.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For him and his generation, the question is not hypothetical.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Because I believe that humanity has the wisdom and ingenuity, and the collective will to find solutions to combat global warming.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Let us make the right choice today, so that our children and grandchildren can look back and be proud of the direction we have set.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: I would just like to take the opportunity to correct two dates which I mentioned in my speech.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: I think the future is going to be upon us faster than we think.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I will now describe our plans to make our urban environment more green and sustainable under the City in Nature and Energy Reset pillars of the Green Plan.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As an island city vulnerable to climate change, the development of climate-resilient buildings is crucial to our survival.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Beyond climate adaptation, we must also reduce carbon emissions from our urban environment.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Given our tight land constraints, we must find innovative ways to weave nature into our urban fabric more intensively.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And even as we face developmental pressures, we must strive to protect our most ecologically important areas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Members have also asked about our plans to achieve these goals.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will make a big push on three fronts.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, transforming Singapore into a City in Nature; second, making our buildings, HDB towns and districts even more sustainable; and finally, driving research and development in urban sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Last year, we set out our goal to transform Singapore into a City in Nature.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Nadia Samdin asked for an update on our efforts.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I will give a fuller update at the MND COS debate later today, but I will set out our plans for the future now.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, we are greening our urban areas more intensively.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the same time, we will also enhance about 170 hectares of existing parks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These parks will feature more lush vegetation and natural landscapes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Altogether, Singaporeans can look forward to over 300 hectares of such parks by end-2026 – almost four times the size of the Singapore Botanic Gardens.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will provide 200 hectares of new nature parks by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Singaporeans can immerse themselves in the nature parks’ lush forests and enjoy nature-based recreational activities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our new nature parks also act as buffers to protect our nature reserves against urbanisation, and provide more habitats for native flora and fauna to thrive.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Nadia Samdin and Prof Koh Lian Pin also asked about how we can continue to improve connectivity between our natural spaces.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is a key strategy of our City in Nature vision.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Not just to conserve specific pockets of greenery and nature, but to look at Singapore and our map from an ecological connectivity point of view.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Habitats that are ecologically connected increase the chances of survival for flora and fauna in our city.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That is why we have been strengthening Singapore’s ecological connectivity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are doing so by studying faunal movement patterns and flora dispersal mechanisms and pathways both on land and in the water.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This understanding of the connections between our natural spaces has, in turn, enabled us to conserve key habitats that are important for ecological connectivity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, we recognised that the forests at the future Bukit Batok Hillside Nature Park and Bukit Batok Central Nature Park are important stepping stones between the Bukit Timah Nature Reserve and the future Tengah Forest Corridor.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That is why we dedicated these nature parks as part of the Bukit Batok Nature Corridor.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They will be kept lushly forested, so that they can strengthen not just the area’s green network, but also ecological connectivity between the Nature Reserve and Tengah.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also designated Sisters’ Island as a Marine Park, because modelling studies indicate that it is a key source of coral larvae, which are widely dispersed and enrich other areas in the Southern Islands.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, as I shared with the House last week, we are developing a more comprehensive picture of our islandwide eco-system and connectivity of green and blue spaces, so that we can better consider how specific sites connect to our nature cores, buffers, and corridors.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And we are creating ecological corridors on the ground by doing physical planting, to better connect our green spaces.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, we are planting native trees and shrubs more intensively to re-create forest-like structures along our roads known as Nature Ways, to augment our network of ecological corridors between key habitats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I am glad to share that we will develop new recreational routes across our island, in the next phase of expansion of our Park Connector Network.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will provide more details on these new routes at MND’s COS debate later today.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Together, these moves will not only strengthen ecological connectivity, but also provide Singaporeans with greater access to green spaces close to home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: By 2030, every household will be within a 10-metre walk from a park.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our urban areas will also be naturalised and greened even further.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: By incorporating natural designs and plantings into our parks and streetscapes, they can serve as nature-based solutions to help provide shade, cool the environment, improve air quality, enhance flood resilience and beautify our city.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These are just some of the benefits and outcomes that we hope to see from our City in Nature efforts, which Prof Koh Lian Pin had asked about yesterday.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: One example of this can be seen at Jurong Lake Gardens, our third national garden.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We converted a concrete canal into a series of meandering streams with vegetated wetlands that play host to charismatic wildlife, such as otters and herons.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Such naturalised waterways can help slow down water runoff from surrounding areas, reducing the risk of flash floods.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will naturalise more waterways and waterbodies in parks and gardens in this manner as part of our City in Nature efforts.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are conserving our rich biodiversity too, through habitat restoration and species recovery programmes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, as part of our Marine Conservation Action Plan, we placed purpose-built intertidal pools along a barren stretch of seawall, to provide a habitat during low tide for coastal and marine biodiversity to thrive.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are also working with the community to improve how we co-exist with nature and wildlife, by taking a science-based approach towards wildlife management and harnessing both ecological and social tools to minimise human-wildlife conflict.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The active support of the community is crucial to making our City in Nature vision a reality.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That is why we are working with the community across many areas, from continuing to support community gardening, to the OneMillionTrees movement.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We appreciate that many Singaporeans have a strong sense of affinity for our existing green spaces.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That is a good sign of the maturity of a City in Nature.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, the OneMillionTrees movement is not merely a quantitative effort to increase our island's tree numbers or to engage in ornamental planting.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Instead, it underpins our qualitative transformation into a City in Nature – not just nature, but a city as well.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Indeed, even if we were to hypothetically forgo some of our people's needs and halt all new development on vegetated land, we would still need to plant more trees at an accelerated rate in light of our climate challenges.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The trees we are planting offer us many benefits.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I mentioned some of them just now – mitigating urban heat to increase our climate resilience, providing more habitats for local biodiversity in our existing green spaces and strengthening our eco-systems' resilience by creating ecological corridors.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Indeed, even in the heart of our core forests, we are doing tree planting and forest restoration, as part of our OneMillionTrees movement.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the same time, we are also proactively removing invasive species, like Albizia trees, Dioscorea and oil palms, to allow our native rainforests to regenerate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is because we need to actively manage our forests to make them stronger.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: By doing so, we are assisting our early secondary forests to transition into more mature and diverse rainforests over time and improving habitats for native biodiversity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These efforts strengthen the resilience of our forest landscapes to climate change.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is painstaking, long-term work and we are deeply appreciative of our community of volunteers who have rolled up their sleeves and have been working alongside us to make our native eco-systems healthier and more resilient.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But even as we continue greening Singapore, we must also continue to meet our people's needs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This balancing act between conservation and development will become even more challenging given our tight land constraints.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Prof Koh Lian Pin also spoke about our Environmental Impact Assessment or EIA framework and public consultation on preserving green spaces.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will take them into consideration as we continue our study.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And as I mentioned earlier, NParks will continue to study and model our biodiversity's movement patterns, to inform our understanding of ecological connectivity across Singapore and how to strengthen it.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, studying ecological connectivity, in a city and urban environment, to infuse City in Nature all through our urban landscape.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Given Singapore's land constraints, we will not be able to keep every vacant land undeveloped.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As a city-state, we must cater for everything that a country needs within just our city limits.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We need space to continue meeting our people's needs, ranging from industry and food production, to more public housing for Singapore families.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, we adopt a range of strategies to make good use of existing land, as good stewards ought and in so doing, enable us to retain more green spaces of significant biodiversity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are also committed to engaging stakeholders, including members of the public and the nature community, further upstream in our planning process and will work with them at suitable platforms to identify these areas of interest.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleague Minister Indranee Rajah will share more about our plans to discuss these issues with Singaporeans as part of our national conversations on long-term land use planning, at MND's COS debate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Buildings account for over 20% of our emissions, so we need to push hard to make our city more sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To achieve this, we will use cleaner energy and increase our energy efficiency.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked for an update on the Singapore Green Building Masterplan.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the past year, BCA and the Singapore Green Building Council have worked together to develop the next edition of the Singapore Green Building Masterplan together with industry stakeholders and the community.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is an existing target, to ensure that the majority of buildings that we use in our everyday lives will be sustainable and energy efficient.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To date, we have made good progress by greening over 43% of our buildings, but we have more to do.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Beyond that, we must push more owners of buildings to pursue best-in-class standards and become Super Low Energy buildings, or SLE buildings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: SLE buildings, which achieve at least 60% improvement in energy efficiency compared to 2005 levels, represent the next wave of our green building movement.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Government will take the lead in SLE buildings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In so doing, we will build industry capability to develop SLE buildings and provide more use cases for the private sector to take reference from.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will ramp up research and innovation efforts to push the boundaries of energy efficiency and accelerate deployment of cost-effective green technologies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Since 2014, our Green Buildings Innovation Cluster (GBIC) programme has supported the research, prototyping and demonstration of green building technologies and helped to bring these solutions to market.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are seeing how we can further enhance funding support for GBIC to help us achieve this ambitious third target.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Sustainability has always been integral to our transformation plans for the Built Environment and we should build on the green movement to drive transformation across the entire value chain and create more opportunities for our firms and our local workforce.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Minister of State Tan Kiat How and I will elaborate on how we plan to do so at MND's COS debate later.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Beyond individual buildings, we also want our towns and our districts to be more sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our new HDB towns will be greener and more sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, Tengah will have centralised cooling systems, electric vehicle charging points and extensive deployment of solar panels.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB is also incorporating technology into the design of towns to improve ventilation and reduce heat gain.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Within their homes, residents will be able to use technology and apps to monitor and optimise the use of their home appliances and equipment, enabling them to conserve electricity, save money and participate in our sustainability efforts too.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Members also asked about our plans to make existing towns more sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MND and MSE are working together to turn every town into an Eco Town, by encouraging residents to live more sustainably.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will achieve this through both technology and design.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, we are using smart LED lights to reduce energy use, doubling total solar capacity on HDB rooftops and converting the top decks of suitable multi-storey carparks into urban farms, community gardens and green landscapes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Since we announced the Green Towns Programme last year, we have made good progress.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So far, HDB has called or awarded tenders to implement solar panels on more than 5,700 HDB blocks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Installation of these solar panels is in progress and will be completed in the next two to three years, achieving more than 50% of our 2030 solar capacity target of 540 megawatt-peak.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB and SFA have also awarded tenders for urban farming at nine multi-storey carparks and will be working closely to do more.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In addition, residents or organisations with interesting ideas to promote sustainability can tap on MSE's Eco Fund for their initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And if these prove workable, MND and MSE will work together to see if these can be scaled to more HDB estates under the Green Towns Programme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will share more about our efforts to enhance liveability and strengthen predictive maintenance in housing estates at MND's COS.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are also developing eco-friendly districts as demonstration projects to show how it can be done.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, Jurong Lake District will be developed as a model sustainable mixed-use district.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Future developments in the District will seek to meet higher sustainability targets that are above our national goals, where possible.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We envision the District to be a model for how innovative solutions and technology can enable a more liveable, sustainable and healthier urban environment.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It can also serve as a testing ground for such innovative urban solutions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Indeed, innovation enables us to keep moving forward on the journey of sustainable development.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That is why R&D is part of our long-term strategy for urban sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Since its launch in 2017, our Cities of Tomorrow (CoT) research and development programme has supported R&D that helps to address urban sustainability challenges.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, HDB and NUS are exploring urban designs that harness solar heat to create temperature differences that enhance air movement through a building.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This can help create natural drafts to cool the environment, thereby minimising residents' air-conditioning needs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will build on the good progress of CoT and extend it for another five years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan and Ms Nadia Samdin asked how we will support R&D into nature-based solutions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Sustainability is a marathon which we cannot run alone.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We must be in it for the long haul – to be responsible stewards not just for our children, but for their children after them.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In that spirit, let us come together: to push ahead in the next bound of our sustainability journey, to make the Green Plan a reality, and to build a Singapore that we can be even prouder of.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond specific policies, we want to instill a broader mindset change and new environmentally conscious habits.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These will take time to take root in our society.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must start young and inculcate these mindsets in our students through education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members have highlighted this in their speeches, including Mr Abdul Samad, Miss Cheng Li Hui, Ms Nadia Samdin, Dr Shahira Abdullah and Mr Xie Yao Quan.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Environmental education is not new in our schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is part of the curriculum and many schools have programmes to help our students learn to be more environmentally conscious.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will build on our foundation and take it further.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The term "stewardship" represents our individual and collective responsibility to take good care of the environment – not just in the short term, but always with an eye for the future and for future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Doing so requires responsible and informed decision-making, and choosing to do what is good and right through our daily habits.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It also entails an innovative spirit and a mindset of growth, where we can pioneer new ways of doing things in caring for the environment.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through this Eco Stewardship Programme, we aim to inculcate informed and responsible sustainability habits in our students for life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We aim to empower them to make a positive difference in their schools, in their homes and in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Environment and climate change education is already integrated into subjects like Science, Geography and Social Studies.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin and Miss Cheng Li Hui highlighted, we can do more to enhance the teaching and learning of sustainability in both the Sciences, and the Humanities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, in the new upper Secondary Geography syllabus, the topics will be organised around the theme of sustainability where students will understand the impact of sustainability issues.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also refresh and strengthen the Singapore perspective on sustainable development.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To make the learning come alive, we will develop more learning resources which feature sustainability initiatives within our school environment.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These learning resources will help students connect their learning to their actual lived experience in schools, and make the learning more authentic and engaging.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will improve energy efficiency of all our school campuses.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will embark on a programme to gradually have LED lights as the main light source in our classrooms, and more energy-efficient Direct-Current fans.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some schools have already actively harnessed sustainability features within their campuses to enrich students learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, I visited Commonwealth Secondary School recently.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They have several eco-habitats, including the Rainforest, the Stream and the Wetland.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These outdoor classrooms provide students with real eco-systems that they can study and observe.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Students also plant their own vegetables in the school’s nursery, which are harvested for the canteen’s use.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through this immersive environment, students develop a better appreciation for nature and biodiversity.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MOE will, therefore, continue to green our schools and testbed new innovations, so that our school buildings can be more sustainable and our school campuses can become learning laboratories for our students to see sustainability in practice.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond academic learning and infrastructure, we also need to instill the right habits in our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This includes encouraging them to reduce waste, to recycle right and to reduce energy use as a matter of habit.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The third C is, therefore, about Culture and through the Eco-Stewardship Programme, we aim to strengthen the eco-culture in schools towards sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will build on existing efforts to instill daily habits of environmental consciousness.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will expand our everyday responsibilities to include sustainability habits.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It could be simple activities like switching off lights and fans upon leaving the classrooms and, in fact, some schools have also encouraged students to reduce and recycle food waste.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, Elias Park Primary School has a food waste management programme, where students are taught and encouraged to order only what they can finish and use the bio-digesters in the canteen for food waste recycling.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will expand such good practices to more schools and pilot ways for students to see that their daily habits can make a discernible impact on the environment.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also help students champion sustainability mindset and practices through leadership opportunities so that they can encourage their peers and friends towards more sustainable living.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Building a culture of sustainability requires schools, families and the community to complement one another’s efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The learning from schools will reinforce our community efforts, and in turn, will encourage and cultivate more good habits to create a ripple effect on society.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Eco Stewardship Programme will also encompass the Community and that is our fourth C.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Schools are part of a larger community eco-system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will work closely with partners, across different Government agencies and also with the private and people sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will widen and enhance the platforms for students to participate in meaningful community projects to care for the environment and to promote sustainable living.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MOE will also work with partners to strengthen students’ awareness of future “green jobs”.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Dr Shahira Abdullah suggested a greater push for youths to consider a career in the environmental and sustainability sector.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I agree that this is, indeed, a growing sector where we can raise awareness and appreciation amongst young people of the opportunities in this space.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we are equipping our teachers and school Education and Career Guidance counsellors to build students’ awareness of these future opportunities and to help them discover and explore their interests.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These opportunities to explore and prepare our students for more careers in the environmental and sustainability sector will continue beyond schools to our Institutes of Higher Learning, or IHLs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our IHLs will connect students with relevant industry partners through career fairs and the support of Education and Career Guidance counsellors.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They will also work with industry partners to curate internships to expose students to jobs in these sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond a greater push for our youths to consider a career in these sectors, the IHLs are also enhancing green infrastructure and promoting sustainable living initiatives within their own campuses.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, The National University of Singapore has developed a Climate Action Plan 030 to cool its campus by four-degree Celsius and to build a carbon neutral campus.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Other Universities, too, are embarking on their own sustainability journeys.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To further complement these education efforts at the school and IHL level, we will also leverage on the new Science Centre at Jurong Lake District.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Science Centre will champion public education on sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will serve as a showcase for innovative technologies through programmes and exhibits to engage youths and the public.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These schools have already adopted a holistic school-wide approach to sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will work with them to further reduce net carbon emissions from the school buildings and to encourage students to actively reduce their individual carbon footprint.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will learn from their experiences in the pilot, and progressively scale up good and practical solutions across all our schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are not just hard targets in reducing carbon emissions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But, equally, if not more importantly, they are about nurturing our young with the values, skills and know-how to become responsible stewards of the environment.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We hope to see in every student an eco steward for life – where they will have a sensible sensitivity towards the environment, and understand what it means to live sustainably.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I suddenly realise that we do not have enough land for that.

speaker: The Chairman
text: It would have been nice to have a park every 10 metres.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Throughout my speech, I will refer to electric vehicles as EVs, then as for traditional vehicles running on fossil fuels through an internal combustion engine, I will just refer to them as ICEs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There is a net carbon abatement by switching from ICEs to EVs, even if the electricity is generated by fossil fuels.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Today, in aggregate, vehicles on the whole emit about 6.4 million tonnes of CO2-equivalent per year.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If the subset of light vehicles all ran on electricity, the total net carbon abatement would be about 1.5 to two million tonnes per year of CO2-equivalent per year.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, this abatement is about 4% of our total annual emissions, so not insignificant.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Hence, the Singapore Green Plan includes a push for EVs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have a 2040 target to phase out ICEs and have all vehicles run on cleaner energy.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They can be electric, they can be hybrid, hydrogen fuel cell cars, and so on.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As these technologies are evolving rapidly, we will monitor developments closely, and finalise the definition of registrable models well before 2030.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As we know, diesel cars emit PM2.5 and they are even more pollutive.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Several Members have asked what steps will be taken to encourage the take up of EVs in Singapore and meet these targets, the 2030 and 2040 targets.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Some Members have asked whether there are further interim targets.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We used to have a 2040 target; we have just set a 2030 target.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When we gather momentum, maybe we can have more interim targets.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think three aspects will make a difference: taxes, regulations and chargers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The objectives of the COE system and upfront vehicle ownership taxes such as the Additional Registration Fee (ARF), are mostly to manage congestion, to which there is no difference between ICEs and EVs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Therefore, it is not appropriate to waive all or almost all vehicles, on electric cars, as suggested by Dr Lim Wee Kiak, Mr Ang Wei Neng, Mr Lim Biow Chuan.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Technological advancement is narrowing the price differential between ICEs and EVs rapidly.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Experts think price equalisation will happen in 2025 or earlier.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: To give Members an illustration: the main cost of an EV is in the battery.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In 2010, the cost was about US$1,000 per kilowatt-hour of battery power.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, it fell, in 10 years, from US$1,000 per kilowatt-hour to about US$140.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Experts feel that when it reaches about US$100 per kilowatt-hour, this is the tipping point when there will be price equalisation between EVs and ICEs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In the meantime, while the prices are falling, we will offer tax incentives to EV owners.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We introduced the EV Early Adoption Incentive this year.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Together with the enhanced Vehicular Emissions Scheme, the cost of owning an electric car can be lowered by up to $45,000.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Since the start of the year, there have been about 100 new electric car registrations in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is a small number, but we will ramp it up.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for road tax, it is a more complicated matter.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We just implemented a significant downward revision for electric cars from 1 January this year.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For certain models, the reduction is significant, as much as 40%.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Notwithstanding this, we decided to review the matter further.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: A large part of road tax is a luxury tax.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But luxury is subjective and hard to measure.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, for a long time, we have been using engine capacity as a proxy for luxury.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The bigger the engine, the bigger the car, the higher the road tax.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The same approach can be applied to electric cars.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They do not have engine capacity, but we can design the road tax schedule based on propulsion power, measured in kilowatt-hour, as a proxy for luxury.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Then, we should set the electric car road tax schedule such that electric and ICE cars with roughly the same look, feel and level of luxury are subject to the same road taxes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And this is inherently a subjective exercise and would not be very scientific.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But it reflects the policy objective, which is that a large part of road tax is a luxury tax.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And if we take that approach and we then eyeball through the models of ICE and electric cars using their prevailing road tax schedules, we find that for the small and medium electric and ICE cars, their road taxes are quite comparable.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But for the larger cars, they are a little bit off.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: To illustrate, let us compare a 105 kilowatt MG EV, that is the most popular EV in Singapore now, and a 1,800 cc Renault Megane.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Both subject to similar annual road taxes of around $1,000.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But for the slightly larger, mass market segment cars, it becomes a bit off.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: To illustrate again, a 150 kilowatt Hyundai Kona Electric Standard Utility Vehicle (SUV) is subject to about the same road tax as a 2,000 cc Audi Q5 or Q7.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I think Members will agree with me, the level of luxury between the two models is quite different.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The long and short of it is, we will bring down the road taxes of electric cars in the upper band.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And this will make their road taxes comparable to ICE models with a similar look and feel.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Some car enthusiasts have observed that for big electric cars, those 230 kilowatt, 300 kilowatt, the road tax schedule is also a bit off.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: To illustrate, some have told me an electric Porsche Taycan is subject to significantly more road tax than a Porsche Cayenne.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I prefer to leave them alone for now.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: What is important is that we have now established the principles and policy for charging road tax on electric cars.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The second area of work is to improve our regulations and standards.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They are not the latest emojis, they are different kinds of plugs for EVs used around the world.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The set of technical standards and safety precautions that governs the EV charging systems in Singapore is called the Technical Reference 25 (TR25).

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is administered by the Energy Market Authority (EMA).

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: LTA is also leading a comprehensive review of TR25 in partnership with industry players and various stakeholders and experts.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We expect the review to be completed by end of this year.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The idea is to make TR25 friendly to industry development, while ensuring safety.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: While the review is on-going, LTA plans to set up regulatory sandboxes for commercial players to test and introduce new charging solutions.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is very important we get this right, because it will determine the level of private sector involvement in finding solutions to build up the infrastructure and drive EV charging and adoption.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: A couple of Members also raised the issue of disposal and recycling of used EV batteries.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This comes under the regulation of NEA and will be addressed at the MSE's COS speeches later.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If we assume one-third of cars are EVs by 2030, this translates into a EV to charging point ratio of about 5:1.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And this ratio is better than many public estimates of the optimum ratio, which ranges from 10:1 to 5:1.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we are aiming for 5:1 by 2030.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The key to unlocking more charging facilities is to not insist on high-powered, or "fast" charging.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Because that would require a major upgrading of almost all the power substations and the grid infrastructure all over Singapore, as envisaged and raised by many Members.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It would be costly, time-consuming, stall the development and expansion of charging infrastructure, and severely impede the adoption of EVs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I understand why Members like Mr Ang Wei Neng want charging to be faster.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Given a choice, I think we all want charging to be faster.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And I think for most drivers, the deterrent to switch to EVs for now is the sheer lack of charging points.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We can move much faster in making charging points available if we accept that for most users, instead of high-powered "fast" charging, "slow" or "overnight" charging is actually alright.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In US, Europe and Japan, EV users predominantly use slow charging, with fast charging, and they define it as 22 kilowatt and above, estimated to account for 10%-20% of charging demand.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, this requires drivers to change our habits.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Drivers are used to a very quick visit to the petrol kiosks, pump, buy a drink and go.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: After all, we are used to patiently charging all our electronic devices whether they are smart phones, smart watches or laptops, while we sleep, or while we are in office doing work.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For this mindset shift to happen, we will need to make chargers available and accessible.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The average electric car, now, it has a range of 300-500 km, typically and it is increasing.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That should require a typical user to fully charge about once every five days.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, charging points will need to be shared, with different drivers charging on different days and at different times, especially in public car parks.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That way, we will be able to minimise electrical infrastructure upgrades.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We can tap on the spare electrical capacity in all our public carparks and install charging points as quickly as possible.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And where the infrastructure supports it or where we decide to selectively upgrade the infrastructure, fast chargers can then be installed.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And today, we can already find fast chargers in certain petrol kiosks, shopping malls, industrial and commercial premises.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for fleet operators, P2P operators, for example, and in response to Mr Xie Yao Quan, about 60% of our taxis are already petrol hybrids.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Our car fleet operators are committed to 100% cleaner energy fleets by 2040.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But unlike typical car users, fleet operators will need fast charging in order to support their business operators.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These are issues that Government and fleet operators will need to sit down, discuss and try to work out.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But let me say this: fleet operators will need to be prepared to invest in building up the infrastructure to support their operations.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They can amortise the investment over many vehicles over many years of operations.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Cost of electricity will very likely still work out much cheaper than petrol or diesel now.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: How do we go about installing charging points?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Mr Xie Yao Quan suggested, we plan to make it mandatory for carparks in HDB towns, private residences like condominiums and commercial buildings to cater sufficient electrical capacity to support EV charging and ensure that a minimum number of charging points is installed.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we can only do this for new developments or developments undergoing major changes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for existing carparks, if they are in public housing estates, public sector agencies, such as HDB or URA, will drive the installation.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They are, in alphabetical order: Ang Mo Kio, Bedok, Choa Chu Kang, Jurong West, Punggol, Queenstown and Sembawang.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For non-landed private residences, such as condominiums, in fact, mainly condominiums, we will introduce an EV Common Charger Grant to catalyse implementation.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is part of the $30 million allocation announced in the Budget, to kickstart the build-up of EV charging infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But there is another practical problem which Mr Lim Biow Chuan has mentioned.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: To install charging points in condominiums, the management corporations (MCSTs) will need to convene general meetings and seek approval, which may not be forthcoming even with the grant.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There are already a number of EV charging players, such as SP Mobility, Greenlots and Charge+, some of which are prepared to undertake all the upfront installation costs, in return for a period where they can collect charging revenue.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And this covers cost of electricity, the grid charges, installation cost plus their margins.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: What does this translate into – 39 to 50 cents per kilowatt-hour translates to about seven to nine cents per km travelled, which I think is competitive and attractive.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In many countries, inter-city driving is common and that causes a lot of anxiety amongst EV users because they are afraid of battery depletion – in middle of a highway, you run out of battery, you are in trouble.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But with our urban environment, Singapore is quite ideal as a test-bed for the rapid adoption of EVs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We can be at the forefront of this technology, to advance this significant thrust of the Green Plan.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As we face a rising need to tackle climate change and, at the same time, competing higher energy demands from our population and industry, we will have to transition gradually away from natural gas and find low carbon energy sources to meet our needs progressively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: However, Singapore lacks alternative energy such as wind or tidal power, as Ms Yeo Wan Ling pointed out.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our main source of renewable energy is solar energy which has its limitations, due to its intermittency as well as the need for space.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Therein lies the challenge for all of us here in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: How can we obtain energy that is: one, secure and reliable; two, affordable; and three, that is environmentally sustainable for ourselves over the the long haul.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These three objectives constitute our "energy trilemma", as seeking to achieve each will entail trade-offs for the others.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I wanted to set this context in place by explaining further how we will forge ahead in our efforts to incorporate more renewable energy in our energy sources and enhance the efficiency of our power systems, and how we can continue to manage these trade-offs arising from our energy transition and the "energy trilemma", including smoothening price volatility as well as conserving energy together.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are accelerating our efforts to maximise and densify suitable solar deployment spaces, which Mr Liang Eng Hwa has also asked about.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This includes scaling up the deployment of solar panels on rooftops and open spaces, such as reservoirs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Today, as we speak, we are already one of the most solar dense cities, in terms of power generation, in the world.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Nonetheless, we will continue to explore even more innovative ways to deploy solar and maximise solar deployment across all viable sites, such as untapped spaces, including existing land, canals and roads.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For example, Terrenus Energy, together with JTC, will be extending their Solar Land project on Jurong Island to include multiple renewable energies onsite – solar, we are piloting tidal, wave and wind.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Once this project is completed, this will be Singapore's first four-in-one renewable energy site and we could potentially have the highest renewable energy produced per square metre in the world.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As solar deployment increases, we will have to match this with Energy Storage Systems or ESS deployment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In order for us to enable this, EMA is test-bedding innovative solutions with the industry as well as the research community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These stations will have a smart energy management system to integrate solar, energy storage and electric vehicle or EV chargers to help power their operations and provide one of the fastest public EV charging, when ready in the first quarter of 2022.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As we increase solar and ESS deployment, our power system will become more decentralised.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To enhance our capabilities in grid planning, maintenance and asset management, we are developing a digital twin of Singapore's physical electricity grid.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And we are working closely with the industry to progressively upgrade and refresh our physical grid.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is also initiating a cross-border power trade of up to 100MW under the Lao PDR-Thailand-Malaysia-Singapore Power Integration Project or the LTMS-PIP.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will also allow us to tap on the abundance of hydropower and other renewable energies that some of our Southeast Asian neighbours have.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Prof Koh Lian Pin asked what the Government is doing to assess the carbon footprint of our electricity imports.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For the upcoming trial with Malaysia, EMA will put in place steps to verify the cleanliness of our imports, including requiring importers to submit documentary proof of carbon output.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And the cleaner the proposal, the higher they will be scored and the more favourably will they be scored.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But these are just first steps, small steps towards a regional grid.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In MTI, we have plans to import more electricity and these trials will help us learn and build confidence in importing electricity over the longer term, to diversify our energy sources while tapping on clean energy in the source countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat also asked about how we could help our existing power systems to become more efficient.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Singapore, over the middle to long-term, will need and will continue to need and rely on natural gas as we transition towards cleaner energy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are encouraging, therefore, our power generation companies, or gencos, to adopt more efficient technologies for their generation sets through two grant calls for the Genco Energy Efficiency Grant.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will also facilitate the entry of advanced Combined Cycle Gas Turbines (CCGT), which is the most efficient gas-fired generation technology that is available today, for new generation needs or to replace retiring generation sets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These measures will make our economy more sustainable, but they will inevitably involve trade-offs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For instance, while we seek to accelerate solar deployment, our land constraints and the need for back-up storage adds to the costs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked during the Budget debate last week about our plan to step up electricity infrastructure for use by EVs in the coming years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is why we call this prong of the Green Plan an "energy reset" strategy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Because some upgrading of power generation and grid infrastructure will be required.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will pace the upgrading of the infrastructure alongside with the adoption of the EVs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Saktiandi also asked about whether the current low electricity prices would pose a challenge in encouraging consumers to adopt more energy efficient measures to cut down on their electricity usage.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa also asked how importing electricity will impact electricity prices and the considerations that the Government has in managing any price volatility.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Singapore has an open and competitive electricity market where prices rise and fall depending on demand and supply.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As you can see, in red, it represents the long-run marginal cost of producing electricity.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, that is the true cost of what it takes to produce electricity today.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The black line shows the current market's spot price that fluctuates over the last many years.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is the result of over capacity, currently.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This over-capacity situation will likely be alleviated in the near future.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The low electricity prices today are currently also dis-incentivising the generation companies from investing in new plants.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: You can see from the chart, no company that is commercially-run will sell electricity below cost perpetually.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: What we need to do is to prevent a swing from a glut to a severe shortage of capacity, and this will result in sharp price spikes; perhaps, even blackouts as what we saw in Texas just last month.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Besides power generation capacity, electricity prices are also affected by the supply of energy.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Please remember, all of us, we are importing close to 100% of our energy needs today.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In spite of our best efforts to deploy solar energy in Singapore, we will still need to rely on energy imports one way or another, and be subject to global prices, going forward.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Fuel prices had dipped to their lowest levels in the last 20 years due to the COVID-19 pandemic last year, but they are expected to rise, going forward, as global demand recovers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This will also likely cause electricity prices to increase as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: However, "right-pricing" of the energy prices is critical to encouraging prudent use of electricity.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We must adopt energy conservation as a way of life for all of us here in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Besides managing the amount of energy we use, consumers can also help us reduce our carbon footprint by electrification.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Minister Ong has already spoken about our ambitious plan to electrify vehicles.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Another example is how we can switch from using gas to electrical appliances for our cooking.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is also safer as the risk of gas leaks and fires are reduced.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And some of the newer electrical cooking appliances, they do produce very, very good "wok hei", the heat that is required to give you very good hor fun.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: (In Mandarin):   Today, Singapore's energy needs are almost 100% met by imports, mainly of natural gas.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Even with our best efforts in using solar energy, we will still need to rely on energy imports.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The Government will do our utmost in reducing the impact on Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The key is that everyone should conserve energy and make corresponding adjustments to our lifestyles.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Energy conservation must become a way of life for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: (In English): In conclusion, Mdm Chairman, the Government will continue taking a long-term approach in planning our energy needs, while balancing the need to be more environmentally sustainable; ensuring continued energy reliability and security, as well as managing price fluctuations and volatility.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Even when prices do go up, we will do our best to ensure that this gradient is gradual, and the Government will act, where necessary, to minimise excessive surges.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Most fundamentally, it is our exhortation to all of us as fellow Singaporeans, that we must do our part to conserve energy, just like how we conserve water, and we all have to adjust our lifestyles accordingly.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is only when we work together, we can maintain a sustainable, secure, reliable and resilient energy future for all of us.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We tried all ways to keep it going, growing and glowing.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In the next 50 years, we will have a chance to turn this Little Red Dot into a bright green spark – a bright green spark with a new economy, with a new way of life, that will provide our future generations with more options and look back with greater pride.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In an increasingly carbon-constrained future, our personal consumption choices will have greater bearing on the environment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Whether it is choosing to use less air-conditioning, opting for public transport, or purchasing products that are more sustainably produced, all of us – as Minister Tan See Leng said – can adjust some bits of our lifestyle to make this transition.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is a commitment that we can all make.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As Minister Grace Fu said, it is a commitment not just for our own benefit, it is a commitment to our future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This commitment applies not just to individuals but also to corporates.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In a carbon-constrained future, being able to operate and produce more sustainably will be key attributes of successful enterprises.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Increasingly, consumers are much more discerning and place a greater emphasis on sustainable products and services.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is where Enterprise Singapore (ESG) comes in, to help build a strong breed of local enterprises that can harness sustainability as a competitive advantage.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We envision these enterprises to be pioneers and experts in developing solutions that are highly demanded in the green economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Such solutions could range from clean energy, energy efficiency, waste valorisation, water treatment, and so forth.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These enterprises would also possess the mindset that every project they undertake should account for the impact on the environment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: More details on the Enterprise Sustainability Programme (ESP) will be released later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Businesses will be increasingly mindful of the need to embrace Environmental, Social and Governance imperatives in their business practices.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For those new to this journey, we can all start small.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Success is the sum of many small steps, and success belongs to the determined.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As we commit ourselves to a greener future, we must also grow green, by seizing new opportunities in the green economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For traditionally energy-intensive sectors such as petrochemicals and agri-tech, we will need to achieve breakthroughs in carbon and energy efficiency, through innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: With our Industry 4.0 push, we are striving to manufacture more efficiently, using less materials, as well as producing more sustainably for the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our Energy and Chemicals sector is becoming more vital in accelerating our change towards environmental sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It will continue to enable many parts of our economy and it will continue to produce for the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But it will do so much more sustainably.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To get there, we are taking active steps to transform the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Details will also be announced later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are also stepping up decarbonisation and resource optimisation efforts at the plant and systems levels, to transform Jurong Island into a sustainable energy and chemicals park.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Ten years from now, we will also expect that global tourism will have sprung back into a more vibrant sector.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But tourists will have a greater interest in sustainable travel options, for example, eco-friendly hotels and attractions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Through such efforts, we will strengthen Singapore as an exemplary sustainable tourism destination.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Leveraging our strengths as a business hub, we envisage that our future industry mix will comprise more green growth sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We can envisage: Singapore as having leveraged our brand of trust to grow a carbon services sector, with a strong value chain anchored in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: People will turn to us for services including project development, financing, trading, for the credits market, as well as measurement, reporting and verification services.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Singapore’s capabilities and offerings in green financing will also be deepened, to catalyse the growth of new businesses in the green economy, while enhancing our competitiveness as a hub for sustainable solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Just as cashflow is the lifeblood of businesses, financing is a key enabler for the green economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must ensure that our industries are not displaced by sudden economic structural changes.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I am certain Members of this House will agree with us that when we review our carbon prices, we must be very conscious of the impact that this will have on current and future competitiveness and the consequent impact on our jobs and livelihoods for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The transformation of our industries and the rise of the green innovation will germinate new jobs, to help solve sustainability problem statements faced by the region, and globally.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And Singaporeans can take advantage of these bright spots by upskilling and re-skilling ourselves.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We can be better placed to capture these new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We can also help our corporates deliver on their sustainability mandates, and countries to advance their charge towards a more sustainable economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And we will continue to find our place in the green economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We can be a bright green spark, by being an inspiration to the world on how we overcome sustainability-related constraints.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have done so for water over the last 50 years.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have done it also for transportation, and the way we build and organise our city.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are going to do so for energy because that will be a big part of glowing green.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Not just for ourselves but for the whole world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Singapore’s birth and growth have never been defined by circumstances, challenges or constraints.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We endeavour to help others overcome their sustainability constraints, both regionally and globally.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Only then can we pass on a healthy and sustainable portion of these reserves to future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Growing our green economy is also about a stewardship of opportunity.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The bright spots that I mentioned and the ambitions that I have shared are not lofty ideas.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These are potential real outcomes that we believe Singapore and Singaporeans can achieve – together.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, we urge everyone to consider how we can each contribute, how our economy will be greener, our people will be more relevant, and our society, ever resilient.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will be our new normal, our new charge and our new opportunity.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, yes, there is a lot at stake for the environment; but also, for Singapore’s future and our economy and the livelihoods of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But with resolve and cooperation, we think we can go fast, we can go far, and we can go together.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And together we will not only defend this little red dot, we will turn this little red dot into a bright green spark to be an inspiration for future generations and the world.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I was quite excited for a while when Senior Minister said we would reach half of our emissions by 2030 but then he burst my bubble.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But I really hope that we can try to reach net zero emissions by 2050.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: If not, could I ask whether we can at least narrow the timeframe.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, instead of by the second half of the century, which could be 79 years' time, when I was hoping we can actually see net zero emissions within my lifetime.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But if we can at least reduce here, maybe by 2060 or 2070.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: If not, can the Government at least consider to focus it on a per sector basis?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, something like what MOE has done which is that 20% of the schools will achieve carbon neutrality by 2030.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The second question really is for MOE – when can we expect the other 80% of the schools to reach carbon neutrality?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
